root_cause.text: The NVMe host code in `nvme_alloc_admin_tag_set()` failed to release an existing `ctrl->admin_q` during controller reset, so allocating a new admin request_queue orphaned the old queue and leaked it.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (ctrl->admin_q) blk_put_queue(ctrl->admin_q);` before `ctrl->admin_q = blk_mq_alloc_queue(...)`, and the commit message says “When nvme_alloc_admin_tag_set() is called during a controller reset, a previous admin queue may still exist. Release it properly before allocating a new one to avoid orphaning the old queue.”

Release it properly before allocating a new one to avoid orphaning the old queue.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Release any existing admin queue before allocating a replacement to avoid orphaning it during reset or reinitialization.
intent_record.what: The function now checks whether `ctrl->admin_q` is already set before creating a new admin queue, and if so it calls `blk_put_queue(ctrl->admin_q)` immediately before assigning `ctrl->admin_q = blk_mq_alloc_queue(set, &lim, NULL);`. A new explanatory comment was added describing this as cleanup for a previous admin queue, such as one left over from before a reset.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents an existing admin queue from being left referenced and unreleased when a new admin queue is allocated. This avoids leaking or orphaning the prior queue during reinitialization or reset paths, ensuring proper queue lifecycle management.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it adds release of an existing admin queue before allocating a new one, preventing the old `ctrl->admin_q` from being orphaned and leaked during reset/reinitialization.

candidates.rationale: This allocates a new admin request queue without first releasing any existing ctrl->admin_q, which can orphan the old queue during reset/reinitialization and cause a leak.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement allocates a new admin request queue and overwrites ctrl->admin_q without first releasing any existing admin queue, which orphans the prior queue during controller reset/reinitialization and leaks it.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is `nvme_alloc_admin_tag_set()`, and it only allocates a new admin queue with `ctrl->admin_q = blk_mq_alloc_queue(set, &lim, NULL);` followed by cleanup on allocation failure. The vulnerability root cause is that an existing `ctrl->admin_q` was not released during controller reset before allocating a new one, but that pre-existing queue handling is not shown anywhere in this function. The only queue cleanup here is the error path for a failed `fabrics_q` allocation (`blk_mq_destroy_queue(ctrl->admin_q); blk_put_queue(ctrl->admin_q);`), which is not the reset-time fix for replacing an old admin queue. Therefore this snippet does not show the vulnerable reset path and also does not show the fix.
